newsitem.title: GERMANY: Compaq aims at higher European market share.
newsitem.headline: Compaq aims at higher European market share.

text.p: BONN, Germany - Compaq Computer Corp., hoping to rebound after a tough year in Germany, plans to roll out new low-cost personal computers next week aimed at home users, company officials said Friday.
The Presario 2110 computers will offer German consumers complete multimedia systems with sound, video, fax and Internet capabilities for 2,200 marks ($1,200).
The price is almost exactly equivalent to Compaq's U.S. price for the same model, but value-added taxes would boost it higher.
"We expect to make significant market share gains," Toon Bouten, Compaq vice president for consumer products said in an interview.
Last year Compaq had too few offerings in the German consumer segment, with its cheapest model priced at 3,500 marks ($2,080), he said. The Presario will help correct that this year, he added.
Still, analysts were not convinced the new machines would strengthen Compaq against established German suppliers Vobis Microcomputer AG and Siemens Nixdorf Informationssysteme AG.
"I would not assume it will be easy for Compaq to regain market share," said James Bates at market researcher Context in London.

The company said it would release the Presario 2110 -- which uses a processor from Cyrix Corp. instead of Intel Corp. -- first in Germany, France, Britain, Austria and the Netherlands. They should arrive in other countries over the next six months.
